topic: Mastering Limits: From Intuition to Precision and Shortcuts

outline.topic: Mastering Limits: From Intuition to Precision and Shortcuts

sections.title: The Intuitive Foundation: The 'Zeno's Rabbit' Approach
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a limit by visualizing a rabbit jumping toward a carrot placed at x=2. The rabbit halves its distance with every jump. Even if it never technically 'reaches' the coordinate, we can define its 'target' position. Emphasize that a limit describes behavior near a point, not at the point itself.
sections.example: A rabbit at x=1 jumps to 1.5, then 1.75, then 1.875. As the number of jumps n approaches infinity, the position approaches 2.

sections.title: The Epsilon-Delta Rigor: Building the 'Safety Bubble'
sections.content: Transition from intuition to the formal definition. Use a graphical representation: a 'target' range epsilon (ε) on the y-axis, and a corresponding 'input' range delta (δ) on the x-axis. Explain that for any tiny error margin (ε) we choose, we can find a tiny input window (δ) that keeps the function inside the target.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'box' around the limit point (L); shrinking the height of the box (ε) forces the width (δ) to shrink to maintain function inclusion.

sections.title: L'Hôpital's Rule: The Shortcut for Indeterminate Forms
sections.content: Introduce the problem of 0/0 and ∞/∞ cases. Explain that when algebraic simplification (factoring) fails, we use the derivative of the numerator and denominator to find the slope ratio at the target point. Prerequisite: Students must understand that local linearity (derivatives) mirrors the behavior of functions near a point.
sections.example: Calculating the limit of (sin x)/x as x -> 0. Visualizing the tangent lines of f(x)=sin x and g(x)=x at x=0; both share a slope, thus the limit is the ratio of their derivatives: cos(0)/1 = 1.

sections.title: Synthesis & Summary
sections.content: Review the progression: Limit (Where are we going?) -> Epsilon-Delta (How certain are we?) -> L'Hôpital (How do we compute it quickly?). Provide a high-level visual map connecting these concepts.
sections.example: A 'Limit Toolbox' graphic: Intuition for 'Understanding,' Epsilon-Delta for 'Verification,' and L'Hôpital for 'Efficiency'.

storyboard.title: The Intuitive Foundation: The 'Zeno's Rabbit' Approach
lecture_lines: Imagine a rabbit jumping halfway toward a carrot.
Each jump brings the rabbit closer to x=2.
The distance halves, yet it never reaches two.
We define the limit as its target position.
A limit describes behavior near a point.
animations: Create a number line with a carrot at x=2. Use [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/carrot.png]. Color carrot #FF8C00.
Create a rabbit at x=0 using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/rabbit.svg]. Use #8B4513 for the rabbit. Animate rabbit to x=1.
Animate rabbit [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/rabbit.svg] to x=1.5, then x=1.75, showing jumps halve.
Draw a dashed vertical line at x=2 labeled 'Limit'. Use #FFFFFF.
Highlight the rabbit's [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/rabbit.svg] proximity to x=2 using a glow effect in #FFD700.

storyboard.title: The Epsilon-Delta Rigor: Building the 'Safety Bubble'
lecture_lines: We formalize limits using epsilon and delta.
Epsilon defines our target error range vertically.
Delta defines the required input range horizontally.
A smaller epsilon forces a tighter delta.
This ensures the function stays within limits.
animations: Draw a Cartesian plane with a function curve f(x). Color curve #00BFFF.
Add a target value L on the y-axis. Draw a horizontal epsilon band [L-eps, L+eps] in #FF0000 with 30% opacity.
Project epsilon band to x-axis to find delta interval [c-delta, c+delta] in #32CD32 with 30% opacity.
Shrink the epsilon band vertically; show the delta interval shrinking accordingly on the x-axis.
Highlight the point (c, L) where the function is 'trapped' by these bounds. Display a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bubble.svg] at (c, L) to emphasize the limit definition.

storyboard.title: L'Hôpital's Rule: The Shortcut for Indeterminate Forms
lecture_lines: Algebra fails for indeterminate forms like 0/0.
L'Hôpital's Rule uses derivatives as a shortcut.
We compare slopes of numerator and denominator.
animations: Display 0/0 on screen. Flash it in #FF4500 to indicate error. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg]
Display f(x)/g(x) and transform it to f'(x)/g'(x) using a smooth morph animation.
Animate two tangent lines on the function curves at the point of interest using #FFFF00 and #00FF00.

storyboard.title: Synthesis & Summary
lecture_lines: Limits help us understand behavior near points.
Epsilon-delta provides the rigour we need.
L'Hôpital's Rule offers an efficient shortcut.
animations: Display a map connecting the three concepts (Intuitive, Rigorous, Shortcut). Use a tree layout with nodes in #87CEEB.
Highlight the 'Zeno's Rabbit' node using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/rabbit.svg]. Flash #FF8C00 to link to the foundation.
Highlight the 'Epsilon-Delta' and 'L'Hôpital' nodes in sequence to show completion. Use #FFFFFF to blink nodes.
